summary: Clean on SEC. The three modules are thin @proxy wrappers that forward arguments verbatim to _call_lib_func; they introduce no caller-controlled buffer reads/writes, no string copies, no length arithmetic, no format strings, and no path handling. SQL passed to sqlite3_exec / sqlite3_prepare_v2 is caller-owned by documented contract and numbox performs zero interpolation, so no injection surface is introduced here. The signature widths examined match the C API (prepare_v2 nByte and sqlite3_malloc size are C int -> int32; sqlite3_free(void*) -> void(intp); exec errmsg out-param is a pointer). The errmsg / expanded_sql / exec-errmsg lifetime-and-free contracts that could otherwise cause use-after-free or leaks are caller responsibilities and are documented at the binding sites.
